nominations.discovery: for the development of next-generation sequencing techniques
key_papers: D.R. Bentley et al., Nature, 2008: Accurate whole human genome sequencing using reversible terminator chemistry
nominations.rationale: Their development of sequencing-by-synthesis utilizing fluorescently labeled reversible terminators enabled massive parallelization of DNA sequencing. This breakthrough fundamentally transformed genomics and biochemistry by reducing the time and cost of sequencing by orders of magnitude.

nominations.discovery: for the discovery and development of atom transfer radical polymerization
key_papers: J.S. Wang, K. Matyjaszewski, Journal of the American Chemical Society, 1995: Controlled/living radical polymerization. Halogen atom transfer radical polymerization promoted by a Cu(I)/Cu(II) redox process

M. Kato et al., Macromolecules, 1995: Polymerization of Methyl Methacrylate with the Carbon Tetrachloride/Dichlorotris-(triphenylphosphine)ruthenium(II)/Methylaluminum Bis(2,6-di-tert-butylphenoxide) Initiating System
nominations.rationale: This catalytic process allows for the precise construction of complex macromolecular architectures with defined molecular weights and low polydispersity. It has become one of the most widely used techniques for synthesizing advanced polymers for applications in materials science and medicine.

nominations.discovery: for the discovery and development of semiconductor photocatalysis for water splitting
key_papers: A. Fujishima, K. Honda, Nature, 1972: Electrochemical Photolysis of Water at a Semiconductor Electrode
K. Domen et al., Nature, 2020: Photocatalytic water splitting with a quantum efficiency of almost unity
nominations.rationale: Their pioneering work established the chemical foundations for using solar energy to drive the splitting of water into hydrogen and oxygen. This provides a critical pathway toward sustainable chemical energy conversion and green hydrogen production.

nominations.discovery: for the development of self-assembled monolayers and soft lithography
key_papers: R.G. Nuzzo, D.L. Allara, Journal of the American Chemical Society, 1983: Adsorption of bifunctional organic disulfides on gold surfaces
Y. Xia, G.M. Whitesides, Angewandte Chemie International Edition, 1998: Soft Lithography
nominations.rationale: By establishing the principles of molecular self-assembly on metal surfaces, they provided chemists with unprecedented control over surface properties. The subsequent development of soft lithography translated this fundamental physical chemistry discovery into a versatile tool for nanofabrication and microfluidics.

nominations.discovery: for the development of next-generation DNA sequencing technologies
key_papers: Bentley et al., Nature, 2008: Accurate whole human genome sequencing using reversible terminator chemistry
nominations.rationale: Their development of reversible terminator sequencing enables fast, cost-effective, and massive-scale reading of genomes. This transformed biochemistry and medicine by making large-scale genomic analysis a routine tool.

nominations.discovery: for their discoveries concerning the chaperone-mediated folding of proteins
key_papers: Ostermann et al., Nature, 1989: Protein folding in mitochondria requires complex formation with hsp60 and ATP hydrolysis
Martin et al., Nature, 1991: Chaperonin-mediated protein folding at the surface of groEL through a molten globule-like intermediate
nominations.rationale: They established that proteins do not always fold spontaneously, but often require specialized molecular machines called chaperonins to reach their functional three-dimensional structures. This paradigm shift was critical for understanding cellular homeostasis and protein misfolding diseases.

nominations.discovery: for the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-heteroatom bond formation
key_papers: Guram et al., Angewandte Chemie International Edition, 1995: A Simple Catalytic Method for the Conversion of Aryl Bromides to Arylamines
Louie and Hartwig, Tetrahedron Letters, 1995: Palladium-catalyzed synthesis of arylamines from aryl halides
nominations.rationale: Their independent development of transition-metal catalyzed cross-coupling methods to form carbon-nitrogen and carbon-oxygen bonds revolutionized organic synthesis. These robust chemical tools are now indispensable in the discovery and large-scale manufacturing of pharmaceuticals.

nominations.discovery: for their discoveries of chemical communication in bacteria
key_papers: Fuqua, Winans, and Greenberg, Journal of Bacteriology, 1994: Quorum sensing in bacteria: the LuxR-LuxI family of cell density-responsive transcriptional regulators
Surette, Miller, and Bassler, PNAS, 1999: Quorum sensing in Escherichia coli, Salmonella typhimurium, and Vibrio harveyi
nominations.rationale: They discovered how bacteria use chemical signaling molecules to monitor population density and coordinate collective behaviors, a process known as quorum sensing. Understanding this chemical language provides novel targets for anti-microbial therapies and explains complex microbial ecology.

nominations.discovery: for the development of lipid nanoparticles for the delivery of macromolecular therapeutics
key_papers: Semple et al., Nature Biotechnology, 2010: Rational design of cationic lipids for siRNA delivery
Cullis and Hope, Molecular Therapy, 2017: Lipid Nanoparticle Systems for Enabling Gene Therapies
nominations.rationale: Their pioneering contributions to the design and synthesis of nanoscale lipid and polymer vehicles enabled the clinical application of nucleic acid therapies. This chemical foundation was the critical enabling technology for the rapid deployment of mRNA vaccines.

nominations.discovery: for the development of ab initio molecular dynamics
key_papers: Car, R., Physical Review Letters, 1985: Unified approach for molecular dynamics and density-functional theory
nominations.rationale: The Car-Parrinello method revolutionized theoretical chemistry by combining quantum mechanical density functional theory with classical molecular dynamics. This approach enabled the accurate simulation of complex chemical systems, liquids, and solid-state materials at finite temperatures.

nominations.discovery: for the invention of reversible terminator DNA sequencing
key_papers: Bentley, D. R., Nature, 2008: Accurate whole human genome sequencing using reversible terminator chemistry
nominations.rationale: Their development of reversible terminator chemistry enabled high-throughput, massive parallel sequencing of DNA. This transformed biochemistry and genomics by making whole-genome sequencing fast and affordable.

nominations.discovery: for the development of controlled/living radical polymerization
key_papers: Wang, J. S., Journal of the American Chemical Society, 1995: Controlled/living radical polymerization. Atom transfer radical polymerization in the presence of transition-metal complexes

Kato, M., Macromolecules, 1995: Polymerization of Methyl Methacrylate with the Carbon Tetrachloride/Dichlorotris-(triphenylphosphine)ruthenium(II)/Methylaluminum Bis(2,6-di-tert-butylphenoxide) Initiating System
nominations.rationale: They independently developed atom transfer radical polymerization, allowing precise control over polymer chain architecture and composition. Their methods are now widely used to synthesize advanced materials, coatings, and biomedical polymers.

nominations.discovery: for foundational contributions to the theory and understanding of proton-coupled electron transfer

people.name: Thomas J. Meyer
people.affiliation: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

key_papers: Hammes-Schiffer, S., Accounts of Chemical Research, 2001: Theoretical perspectives on proton-coupled electron transfer reactions
Meyer, T. J., Chemical Reviews, 1992: Chemical approaches to artificial photosynthesis
nominations.rationale: Their theoretical frameworks and experimental validations elucidated how electrons and protons move concertedly in chemical reactions. This fundamental mechanism is central to biological energy conversion, solar cells, and artificial photosynthesis.

nominations.discovery: for the discovery and development of organic light-emitting diodes

people.name: Ching W. Tang
people.affiliation: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

key_papers: Tang, C. W., Applied Physics Letters, 1987: Organic electroluminescent diodes
nominations.rationale: Tang and Van Slyke demonstrated highly efficient electroluminescence from organic thin films, launching the field of organic electronics. Their discovery underpins modern display technologies and energy-efficient lighting.
